crime: All winter, {WITCH_NAME} kept the fire in the lounge fireplace burning on the same logs, and every cold evening she warmed a blanket at it. One girl read beside that fire each night under the warm blanket, by a tallow candle of her own that she let burn down to its brass ring.

On the first warm evening, in the dining hall, the girl picked up her candle to take it to the library. {WITCH_NAME} offered her one of her own, one that would never burn down. "It's warm enough tonight," the girl said. "I like mine to burn down."

{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had only ever come home in the cold months, and on the first warm morning she walked out past the stove her daughter had kept burning all night. People, {WITCH_NAME} learned, stay as long as the fire.

Just before eight, she carried the warmed blanket up to the library, where the girl sat reading at her desk by her candle. She pressed the blanket over the girl's face from behind until the girl was still. Then she pinched the wick straight. The candle had burned a quarter hour down from the top; she left it lit, and from then on it burned without getting any shorter.
From eight until half past nine, she sat with the girls at the lounge fire.

At half past nine, a prisoner going up for a book found the girl dead at her desk, the candle still burning a quarter hour down from the top. The prisoners reckoned she had lit it at a quarter past nine and died after that, while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them the whole time.

But after an hour of working by its light, one prisoner looked at the candle again. It was still a quarter hour down from the top. In the trial court, the prisoners understood: the girl's candle was burning like {WITCH_NAME}'s fire. It had stopped getting shorter when she pinched the wick, before eight.
fields.epitaph: The girl would have come back to the fire with the first frost.
fields.epithet: Keeper of the Fire for Whoever Might Come Back
execution: The execution stand raises a tallow candle as tall as the trial court, set in a brass ring. She is set into the wax at its foot, her back to the shaft. Far above her, the candle burns down, and hot tallow runs down the shaft onto her head and shoulders. The flame comes down to her. The tallow coating her catches, and the fire spreads over her. The candle burns down to its brass ring and goes out on its own, leaving a thread of smoke above her still head.

magic.name: Undying Flame
magic.text: Any fire she lights or tends burns on without ever using up its fuel.
